correctness.rationale: The occupied-row/column domination criterion and line-graph connectivity equivalence are immediate and complete. Cycle-edge deletion forces minimal connected supports to be trees. A spanning-both-sides tree permits deleting a leaf while preserving the opposite full side. For exactly one full side, minimality is equivalent to forbidding leaves on the proper side. The weighted matrix-tree cofactor is evaluated explicitly and its surjective-word coefficients give m^(b-1) b! S(m-1,b); the exponential formula gives every connected set. Exhaustive independent direct-subset checking on 190277 nonempty subsets across eleven labeled boards matches every coefficient and each minimality classification, but the general proof is independent of these tests.

value.rationale: Inclusion-minimal connected domination is a natural global and nonmonotone extremal set system; the theorem classifies every solution, counts each possible cardinality via Stirling numbers, derives an all-connected-set generating function, and proves an exact growing forbidden size interval n>=2m. It supplies structural and quantitative data strictly beyond the known ordinary domination polynomial and scalar minimum, without claiming that standard enumeration tools are novel.
